subject: maths
title: Advanced 10 · Test 2
summary: A 15-question test on trapeziums and composite areas, circles, and the volume and surface area of prisms.
body: This test covers Advanced 10 · Measurement: the area of trapeziums, kites and composite shapes; the circumference and area of circles and parts of circles; and the volume and surface area of prisms, including capacity in litres. It has 15 questions and takes about 25 minutes. Work with no notes. You may use a calculator only for questions that tell you to use π ≈ 3.14. Read each question carefully, check your units, and look closely at any diagram — they are drawn to scale, but always use the measurements given.

questions.prompt: The circle in the diagram has a radius of 7 cm. Find its exact circumference.
questions.explanation: C = 2πr = 2 × π × 7 = 14π cm. 49π is the area, πr².

mistakes.A: Step 1: π × 7 uses the radius in C = πd — double the radius.
mistakes.B: Step 1: π × 7² is the area, not the circumference.
mistakes.D: Step 2: you doubled twice — 2πr uses r = 7.

questions.diagram_alt: A circle with centre O and a radius of 7 cm marked

questions.topic: Volume and surface area of prisms
questions.prompt: The prism in the diagram has a cross-section of area 25 cm² and is 8 cm long. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: V = 25 × 8 = 200 cm³. 100 cm³ halves as if it were a triangle formula, but the area of the cross-section is already given.

mistakes.C: Step 2: no ½ — the cross-section area is already 25 cm².
mistakes.D: Step 2: multiply the area by the length; don't divide.

questions.diagram_alt: A prism 8 cm long with a shaded five-sided cross-section labelled A = 25 cm²

questions.topic: Area of composite shapes and trapeziums
questions.prompt: Find the area of the trapezium in the diagram. Its parallel sides are 9 cm and 15 cm, and they are 8 cm apart.
questions.explanation: ½ × (9 + 15) × 8 = 96 cm². 192 cm² forgets the ½.

mistakes.A: Step 3: halve — two trapeziums make (a + b) × h.
mistakes.C: Step 1: add the parallel sides; don't multiply all three.
mistakes.D: Step 2: multiply by the height — you added all three lengths.

questions.diagram_alt: A trapezium with parallel sides 9 cm (top) and 15 cm (bottom) and a dashed perpendicular height of 8 cm

questions.topic: Area of composite shapes and trapeziums
questions.prompt: A rhombus has diagonals of 14 cm and 10 cm. What is its area?
questions.explanation: ½ × 14 × 10 = 70 cm². 35 cm² multiplies half of each diagonal (7 × 5), which gives only half of the true area.

mistakes.A: Step 3: the rhombus is half of its rectangle — halve.
mistakes.B: Step 2: multiply the diagonals; you added them.
mistakes.C: Step 2: use the whole diagonals (14 and 10), not half of each.

questions.prompt: Using π ≈ 3.14, find the area of the semicircle in the diagram, which has radius 5 cm.
questions.explanation: Half of 3.14 × 5² = half of 78.5 = 39.25 cm². 78.5 cm² is the whole circle.
steps: A semicircle is half a circle.

mistakes.A: Step 3: that is the full circle — halve it.
mistakes.B: Step 1: π × 5 is half the circumference, not an area.
mistakes.D: Step 1: 5 cm is the radius — don't square 10.

questions.diagram_alt: A semicircle with its radius of 5 cm marked along the straight edge

questions.topic: Volume and surface area of prisms
questions.prompt: Find the surface area of the triangular prism in the diagram. Its cross-section is a right-angled triangle with sides 9 cm, 12 cm and 15 cm, and it is 10 cm long.
questions.explanation: Two triangles: 2 × ½ × 9 × 12 = 108 cm². Rectangles: (9 + 12 + 15) × 10 = 360 cm². Total 468 cm². 360 cm² forgets the two ends.
steps: Each triangle: ½ × 9 × 12 = 54 cm², so two ends = 108 cm².

mistakes.B: Step 3: add the two triangular ends as well.
mistakes.C: Step 1: a prism has TWO triangular ends.
mistakes.D: Step 2: 54 × 10 is the volume. Surface area adds the faces.

questions.diagram_alt: A triangular prism 10 cm long; its cross-section is a right-angled triangle with sides 9 cm, 12 cm and 15 cm

questions.prompt: A round garden bed has a diameter of 4 m. Edging costs $5 per metre. Using π ≈ 3.14, how much does it cost to edge the whole bed?
steps: The edging goes around: C = πd = 3.14 × 4 = 12.56 m.

mistakes.A: Step 1: πd uses the diameter 4, not the radius 2.
mistakes.C: Step 1: the distance around is π × 4, not 4.

questions.topic: Area of composite shapes and trapeziums
questions.prompt: The T-shaped garden in the diagram is 12 m across the top and 10 m tall overall. The top bar is 3 m tall and the stem is 4 m wide. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Top bar: 12 × 3 = 36 m². Stem height = 10 − 3 = 7 m, so stem = 4 × 7 = 28 m². Total 64 m². 76 m² uses 10 m for the stem, counting the overlap twice.
steps: Stem height: 10 − 3 = 7 m, so the stem is 4 × 7 = 28 m².

mistakes.A: Step 2: the stem is only 7 m tall — the top 3 m is already in the bar.
mistakes.B: Step 1: 12 × 10 is the whole box, but the sides under the bar are empty.
mistakes.C: Step 1: adding the outside lengths gives the perimeter, not the area.

questions.diagram_alt: A T-shape: top bar 12 m wide and 3 m tall, stem 4 m wide, total height 10 m

questions.topic: Area of composite shapes and trapeziums
questions.prompt: A trapezium has an area of 150 cm² and a perpendicular height of 12 cm. One of its parallel sides is 9 cm. How long is the other parallel side?
questions.explanation: ½ × (9 + b) × 12 = 150, so 6(9 + b) = 150, 9 + b = 25 and b = 16 cm. 25 cm stops before subtracting the 9.

mistakes.A: Step 1: you used 12 × (9 + b) = 150 — include the ½.
mistakes.B: Step 3: 25 is the SUM of both parallel sides — subtract the 9.
mistakes.D: Step 3: undo + 9 by subtracting 9, not adding it.

questions.prompt: A sports field is a 40 m by 20 m rectangle with a semicircle on each 20 m end, as shown. Using π ≈ 3.14, find its total area.
questions.explanation: Rectangle 800 m². The two semicircles make a circle with r = 10: 3.14 × 100 = 314 m². Total 1114 m². 2056 m² uses 20 m as the radius.
steps: Two semicircles = one circle, diameter 20, r = 10: 3.14 × 10² = 314 m².

mistakes.B: Step 2: there are TWO semicircles, which together make a full circle.
mistakes.C: Step 2: 20 m is the diameter — the radius is 10 m.
mistakes.D: Step 2: the curved ends are part of the field — add their area.

questions.diagram_alt: A field: a rectangle 40 m long and 20 m wide with a semicircle on each 20 m end

questions.topic: Volume and surface area of prisms
questions.prompt: The prism in the diagram has an L-shaped cross-section: an 8 cm by 6 cm rectangle with a 5 cm by 4 cm corner removed. The prism is 10 cm long. Find its volume.
questions.explanation: Cross-section: 48 − 20 = 28 cm², times 10 = 280 cm³. 480 cm³ forgets the missing corner.

mistakes.A: Step 1: the corner is missing — subtract 5 × 4.
mistakes.C: Step 1: 5 × 4 is the missing piece, not the L-shape.
mistakes.D: Step 2: 28 cm² is one slice — multiply by the 10 cm length.

questions.diagram_alt: A prism 10 cm long with an L-shaped cross-section: 8 cm along the bottom, 6 cm up the left, with inner edges 5 cm and 4 cm

questions.topic: Volume and surface area of prisms
questions.prompt: A water tank is a cylinder with radius 1 m and height 2 m. Using π ≈ 3.14, how many litres does it hold? (1 m³ = 1000 L)
questions.explanation: V = 3.14 × 1² × 2 = 6.28 m³ = 6280 L. 12 560 L uses the circumference 2πr instead of the area πr².

mistakes.A: Step 3: 1 m³ = 1000 L, so multiply by 1000, not 100.
mistakes.B: Step 1: the radius is 1 m — don't square the diameter.
mistakes.C: Step 1: 2πr is the circumference. The cross-section area is πr².

questions.topic: Area of composite shapes and trapeziums
questions.prompt: A trapezium has parallel sides 7 cm and 13 cm and a height of 6 cm. A rectangle, also 6 cm high, has exactly the same area. How wide is the rectangle?
questions.explanation: Trapezium: ½ × 20 × 6 = 60 cm², so the rectangle is 60 ÷ 6 = 10 cm wide — the average of 7 and 13. 20 cm comes from forgetting the ½.
steps: Width = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 cm (the average of the parallel sides).

mistakes.A: Step 1: include the ½ — the area is 60 cm², not 120 cm².
mistakes.B: Step 1: you used the ½ twice (halving the height too).
mistakes.D: Step 3: 60 cm² is the area — divide by the height to get the width.

questions.prompt: A square is drawn inside a circle of radius 10 cm with all four corners on the circle, as shown. Using π ≈ 3.14, find the shaded area between the square and the circle.
questions.explanation: The square's diagonals are both diameters (20 cm), so its area is ½ × 20 × 20 = 200 cm². Circle: 3.14 × 100 = 314 cm². Shaded = 114 cm². 214 cm² wrongly takes the square's side as 10 cm.
steps: The square's diagonals are diameters, 20 cm each. Using the rhombus rule, area = ½ × 20 × 20 = 200 cm².

mistakes.B: Step 2: the square's side is not 10 cm — its diagonals are 20 cm.
mistakes.C: Step 3: 200 cm² is the white square — subtract it from the circle.
mistakes.D: Step 2: that uses the square AROUND the circle (side 20). This square is inside, with diagonals of 20 cm.

questions.diagram_alt: A circle of radius 10 cm with a white square inside whose four corners touch the circle; the four curved pieces between them are shaded

questions.topic: Volume and surface area of prisms
questions.prompt: A model prism uses 50 cm³ of clay. A bigger model of the same shape has every length 3 times as long. How much clay does it need?
questions.explanation: Volume multiplies three lengths, so it grows 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 times: 50 × 27 = 1350 cm³. 450 cm³ multiplies by 9, which is how areas grow, not volumes.
steps: Volume uses three lengths (length, width, height), each × 3.
So the volume is multiplied by 3 × 3 × 3 = 27.

mistakes.A: Step 2: three lengths are tripled, not one — multiply 3 × 3 × 3.
mistakes.C: Step 2: × 9 is for areas (two lengths). Volume uses three.
mistakes.D: Step 2: 3 × 2 is not how scaling works — multiply 3 × 3 × 3.
